title: Is SysML v2 with UML3 a proper basis for OMG SPMS patterns? The Observer pattern in native constructs
setup: Load the UML3 libraries, then tests/cameo-experiments/e22-pattern-observer.sysml, then e22b-pattern-wrong-binding.sysml. The probe maps SPMS 1.4 (formal/26-04-02) onto native SysML v2 and existing UML3 keywords: PatternDefinition -> an abstract #template part def; Role -> an abstract ref #templateParameter feature with a type and a multiplicity; role relationship -> a connection between role features; PatternSection -> a named comment about the pattern; PatternInstance with Bindings -> a specialization that redefines the roles with design types (type level) or a usage that binds the roles to items of a configuration (instance level); PatternObservation -> valued metadata; RelatedPattern with Nature -> a dependency with metadata; the part of Formalisms a model can carry -> requirement definitions satisfied by the pattern instances. Local evidence before the run: the ANTLR validator reports 0 errors, check_names 0 findings, check_rules 0 findings, and R06 reports a class that plays the observable role without redefining notifyObservers (control in the scratchpad).

predictions.claim: e22-pattern-observer.sysml loads with 0 builder errors: every construct is native SysML v2 or an existing UML3 keyword
predictions.why: the same constructs already load in the libraries and examples: #template/#templateParameter (example 01 Repository), connections between features, named comments, valued metadata, dependencies with a body, satisfy requirement ... by, metaobject-typed attributes (UML3DiagramKinds)
predictions.observation: Run 1 failed on the probe's missing import of ControlFunctions (->exists); after the fix both probes load with 0 builder errors.

predictions.claim: The validation engine reports 0 failures for UML3ProbePatternObserver
predictions.why: new here are a part usage typed by an abstract pattern definition, a satisfy relationship whose satisfying feature is an attribute holding a metaobject, a requirement subject typed by KerML::Type, and a connection between abstract reference features; any of them could meet a CATIA Magic rule not exercised so far
predictions.observation: 0 packages flagged; one WARNING in UML3ProbePatternObserver: validateFeatureTypeConformance on subjectType, the metaobject-typed subject of the model-level requirement ('Feature type must conform to the type of its value's result'). It did not stop the evaluation (P5).

predictions.claim: The role features subset UML3Core::templateParameters and the pattern definition specializes the base of #template, so 'all roles of all patterns' is an ordinary subsetting query
predictions.why: the implied relationships of semantic metadata (KerML 9.2.16), verified for #templateParameter in example 01
predictions.observation: G01, G02 true: the role features subset UML3Core::templateParameters; control N01 false.

predictions.claim: e22b-pattern-wrong-binding.sysml loads and validates with 0 failures although EmailNotifier does not conform to the role type Subject
predictions.why: KerML derives the types of a redefining feature from its typings and from the redefined feature, so a non-conforming binding intersects the types instead of violating a rule; if CATIA Magic flags it after all, role binding is checked by the language and a UML3 rule is unnecessary
predictions.observation: e22b loads and validates with 0 results, and the misbound observable role conforms to both Subject (G07) and EmailNotifier (G08) while EmailNotifier does not specialize Subject (N03): a non-conforming binding intersects the types silently, so UML3-PAT-011 needs a rule.

predictions.claim: CATIA Magic can evaluate the model-level requirement SubjectTypeOwnsNotify for the subject OrderService meta KerML::Type (ownedFeature->exists over the reflective KerML library) and returns true
predictions.why: CATIA Magic evaluates '(pkg meta KerML::Package).ownedElement' in the palette customization, but evaluating a requirement's constraint needs an evaluation entry point that has not been found yet; the experiment needs a script that evaluates the constraint through the tool's expression evaluator
predictions.observation: CATIA Magic's evaluation engine (kerml.evaluation.Evaluator, SysML v2 Evaluation Plugin installed) evaluates each satisfy requirement usage to a StructuredValue whose 'result' feature is the verdict: V01 instance-level ObserversAreNotified true, V02 control (three observers) false, V03 model-level SubjectTypeOwnsNotify (ownedFeature->exists over the reflective KerML library) true, V04 control (notifyAll) false. Three attempts were needed to read the verdict from the value API; the engine itself reported no error in any of them. Logs: logs/cameo-e22-p5.log, -p5b.log, -p5c.log; logs/cameo/evaluations.txt.

observations.result: P1 not met: CATIA Magic rejected e22-pattern-observer.sysml with one semantic error, line 50 "Name resolution error: couldn't resolve reference to Element 'exists'". The probe used the arrow invocation ->exists without importing ControlFunctions, which defines it; the official examples import ControlFunctions::* where they use ->forAll. The failed load was cancelled, so e22b could not resolve its import and every hypothesis reported 'not found'. The libraries loaded and validated with 0 failures. This is a defect of the probe, not of the basis: the construct is native. Neither the ANTLR validator nor check_names looked at names inside expressions; check_names now has rule FUNCTION with negative test n25, and calibration on 251 OMG models stays at 0 false positives. The probe now imports ControlFunctions::*.

P1 met: both probes load with 0 builder errors (AS PREDICTED OK). P2 met for errors: the validation engine flags none of the 10 packages; UML3ProbePatternObserver (643 elements) has one WARNING, validateFeatureTypeConformance on subjectType, 'Feature type must conform to the type of its value's result', i.e. on the metaobject-typed subject of the model-level requirement bound to 'OrderService meta KerML::Type'. P3 met: G01 and G02 true (the roles subset UML3Core::templateParameters), control N01 false. P4 met: e22b loads and validates with 0 results (22 elements), and the misbound observable role conforms to both Subject (G07) and EmailNotifier (G08) while EmailNotifier itself does not specialize Subject (N03): a non-conforming binding intersects the types silently. Also G03-G06 and G09 true. 12/12 hypotheses; undo clean.
P5: 4/4 verdicts as predicted (V01 true, V02 false, V03 true, V04 false); undo clean. The run is now the permanent suite cameo-patterns of tools/run_tests.py --cameo.

conclusion: SysML v2 with UML3 is a proper basis for SPMS patterns. The pattern definition, typed roles, role connection, sections, type-level and instance-level instances, observations and relationships all load and validate in CATIA Magic with existing UML3 keywords; the roles are queryable as template parameters; and CATIA Magic's evaluation engine evaluates the pattern's requirements, including a structural conformance requirement over the reflective KerML library, with false controls behaving as false. One behavior needs a UML3 rule: binding a role to a non-conforming type is not an error but narrows the role to an intersection of types (UML3-PAT-011).
